name: He Zhenggang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2009-2026)
forbes_bio: He is the second largest shareholder of Leshan Giantstar Farming & Husbandry, a supplier of leather products.
He stepped down as the company's chairman in August 2023.
He is also a director and the majority shareholder of Shanghai-listed chemicals supplier Sichuan Hebang Biotechnology.
He worked for a city government commercial bureau in Leshan, China from 1971 to 1993 and founded Hebang's predecessor company in 1993.
The company listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange on Dec. 18, 2017.

name: Hartati Murdaya
forbes_bio: Hartati Murdaya is the president director of Central Cipta Murdaya, which she cofounded with her late husband Murdaya Poo, who died in April 2025 at age 84.
Central Cipta Murdaya has investments in engineering, IT, palm oil and plywood.
Her Jakarta International Expo is one of the city's biggest convention centers.
She owns a substantial stake in listed property developer Metropolitan Kentjana where she and her four children have board seats.

name: Cai Hongbin
forbes_bio: Cai Hongbin's fortune comes from his stake in Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine.
Jiangsu Hengrui is one of China's largest pharmaceutical companies, employing more than 20,000 people.
Fellow Chinese billionaire Sun Piaoyang is Hengrui's chairman.

name: Ma Fei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Ma Fei is the chairman of Shenzhen FRD Science and Technology, a supplier of electronics materials.
Ma Fei founded Shenzhen FRD in 2014.
FRD listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2014.

name: Renjun Lu
forbes_bio: Lu is the former chairman of Shanghai Zhezhong Group, a supplier of concrete pipe.
The company's products are used in construction of elevated roads, highways, power plants, ports and bridges.
Lu was once a teacher in Zhelin School in Shanghai.
Lu stepped down as chairman in 2023. The position is succeeded by his son Jiang Lufeng.

name: Ihor Kolomoyskyy
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2007-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2018)
forbes_bio: With fellow Ukrainian billionaire Henadiy Boholyubov, Ihor Kolomoyskyy founded PrivatBank in the early 1990s.
He served as the governor of his native Dnipro region from March 2014 until March 2015, when he was fired by then-president Petro Poroshenko.
In 2016, Ukraine's government nationalized PrivatBank, after an investigation suggested large-scale fraud over a period of ten years.
In Dec 2017, the High Court of London ordered a freeze on some $2.5 billion worth of assets held by Kolomoyskyy and Boholyubov.
Kolomoyskyy was sanctioned by the U.S. State Department in March 2021 for corruption under his watch at the Dnipro region.
Early ally of President Volodymyr Zelensky, whose "Servant of the People" TV show once ran on Kolomoyskyy's TV network, Kolomoyskyy has reportedly had his Ukrainian citizenship stripped.
forbes_facts: Kolomoyskyy reportedly owns four yachts including the 214-foot Trident and the 180-foot Mustique, both registered in the Cayman Islands.

name: Huang Weibin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2023); Hurun China (2021-2022)
forbes_bio: Huang Weibin chairs Shenzhen-listed Marssenger Kitchenware, a supplier of kitchenware.
Huang cofounded the predecessor of Marssenger Kitchenwarein in Zhejiang Province in 2010.
Huang worked for a cashmere factory for near 10 years before the started his own sweater business in 1992.
Sequoia Capital China owned more than 7% of Marssenger after its IPO in Dec. 2020.

name: Kylie Jenner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2019-2020); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2020-2026); Wikidata (2020)
forbes_bio: The reality TV star sold 51% of Kylie Cosmetics to publicly traded Coty, Inc. in January 2019 for $600 million; she pocketed $540 million, pretax.
Documents later showed the business was much smaller than the family claimed for years.
Jenner first appeared on Forbes Billionaires list in March 2019 at age 21; she is now worth roughly $900 million.
Kylie Cosmetics, which had 2019 revenue of $200 million, was built on the back of a social media following that reaches more than 175 million people.
Jenner used $250,000 of her earnings from modeling to pay an outside company for her first 15,000 lip kits, which sold out in minutes in 2015.
One of the family stars on "Keeping Up With The Kardashians," Jenner remains in charge of creative efforts and marketing for Kylie Cosmetics.
forbes_facts: At age 17, two years before starting the business, Jenner trademarked the phrase "Kylie Lip Kits ... For the perfect pout."
Her family's reality TV show, "Keeping up with the Kardashians", premiered when she was just 10 years old.

name: Xu Bingzhong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2022-2023); Hurun Global (2022-2023); Hurun China (2021-2023)
forbes_bio: Xu Bingzhong opened his first English-style Helen's pub in Beijing in 2009.
Today, Hong Kong-listed Helens International Holdings operates more than 800 bars in more than 100 Chinese cities and one in New York.
Helens listed at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2021.

name: Jiagui Deng
forbes_bio: Deng Jiagui is one of the controlling shareholders of Hubei Feilihua Quartz Glass, a supplier of high-purity quartz glass materials.
Deng stepped down as chairman in 2017 after working in the company for 50 years.
Hubei Feilihua Quartz Glass listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2014.
